clue.text: Turbulent girl's best friend? Good chap, if uncouth

parts.note: turbulent water or weather is rough
from the song: diamonds are a girl's best friend, so one such stone

explanation.surface: A stormy-tempered girl wonders whether her best friend is a decent fellow despite his bad manners.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the song title 'Diamonds Are a Girl's Best Friend'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a person of good character beneath unpolished, coarse manners.

clue.text: Snare for the cyclist's foot

definitions.meaning: a toothed bicycle pedal of the cage type, gripping the rider's shoe

explanation.surface: A trap set to catch the foot of someone riding a bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: The device for catching rodents shares its name with a toothed cage pedal that holds a rider's shoe.

clue.text: A shade of grievance

definitions.meaning: an old literary sense: shadow cast by trees
offence or resentment, as in taking it

explanation.surface: A tint or hint of complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: From Latin umbra, shadow, the word once meant shade and now usually means offence taken.

clue.text: Ran swiftly around the loch arrayed like a horse

indicators.note: the word for running fast is placed around the loch's name

parts.note: to hare is to run very fast
Loch Ness, the best-known Scottish loch

explanation.surface: Someone sprinted round a Scottish lake dressed up like a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrayed like a horse' means fitted with tack; 'around' tells you the loch goes inside the word for running fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse is dressed in tack and straps, so one so equipped is fitted out in its gear.

clue.text: In Berlin I take gold for the blood of some high-ups

parts.note: the German word for the first-person pronoun
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A German speaker trades gold for the blood of aristocrats.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'high-ups' are not nobles but the Greek gods, whose veins ran with this fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this ethereal fluid flowed in the veins of the gods instead of blood.

clue.text: Attractive piece with nothing on made the sparks fly

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the device that does so, a noun

parts.note: a lump of iron that attracts metal
the letter O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A glamorous, scantily clad person caused a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with nothing on' suggests nudity; here O is simply added after the attracting piece.
explanation.definitionFit: This generator produced the high-voltage pulses for the ignition sparks in early engines.

clue.text: Closest are in retreat

indicators.note: the word are sits in the word for a hideaway

parts.note: a nest is a snug hideaway
taken as written

explanation.surface: The nearest ones are pulling back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' looks like a verb but is a noun: a snug hideaway, NEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean nearest in distance, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Indicate the fieldsman for a chase in the country

parts.note: to point to something is to indicate it
point is a cricket fielding position near the batsman on the off side

explanation.surface: A cricket captain directs a fielder before a cross-country chase.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, point is a fielding position square of the batsman on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a steeplechase race for amateur riders over farmland, originally from one landmark to another.

clue.text: Drink to the time of revolution

definitions.meaning: a strong ale traditionally brewed in the autumn month
the 1917 Bolshevik seizure of power is named after this month

explanation.surface: A toast to the era of uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian Revolution of 1917 bears the month's name, as did a strong ale brewed then.

clue.text: Rider finds it difficult without a horse

indicators.note: an old sense of without meaning outside, so the word for difficult goes round the rest

parts.note: hard means difficult
gee-gee, a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: A rider without a mount finds things hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider' is the middle name of H. Rider Haggard, author of 'King Solomon's Mines'; 'without' has its old sense of outside, so the word for difficult wraps the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist H. Rider Haggard is linked to his middle name, so the surname is clued by it.

clue.text: Long time in the life of Nicholas Nye

definitions.text: Long time in the life of Nicholas Nye

parts.words: Long time in the life of Nicholas Nye
parts.note: Nicholas Nye is the donkey in Walter de la Mare's poem, so a long period is measured in that animal's lifespan

explanation.surface: A span of years in the life of a man named Nicholas Nye.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicholas Nye is the old grey donkey of Walter de la Mare's poem, so his years are a donkey's.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a very long period, reputedly from the long life of the animal.

clue.text: Sped back to scold and tell

indicators.note: the word for sped is written backwards

parts.note: ran is a synonym of sped
to rate is to scold, an old sense

explanation.surface: Someone hurried back to tell off and inform on another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses RAN to NAR; to rate someone is an old word for scolding them.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount a story is to relate it in order.

clue.text: School eggs offered to the churchman

parts.note: roe is fish eggs
a dean is a senior cleric of a cathedral

explanation.surface: Eggs are served to the priest at a school.
explanation.walkthrough: Roedean is a well-known girls' boarding school near Brighton in England.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a famous English independent school for girls.

clue.text: High points for cool cover in India

parts.note: top means highest or uppermost
two compass points, east and east

explanation.surface: Peaks offer a cool shelter in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High points' looks like one phrase meaning peaks; it splits into TOP and two compass points, E and E.
explanation.definitionFit: This light pith helmet kept the sun off wearers in the hot Indian climate.

clue.text: Train to draw in distinctive fashion

parts.note: to school someone is to train them
a tie is a drawn game

explanation.surface: Someone learns to sketch in a stylish, individual way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw' looks like sketching but means a game that ends level, a TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A striped neckwear pattern worn by former pupils marks them out by their old school.

clue.text: Daughter of Venus holds a hundred musical glasses

indicators.note: the goddess's name holds the numeral inside it

parts.note: Harmonia, daughter of Venus (Aphrodite) and Mars in myth
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: The daughter of the love goddess clutches a hundred singing wine glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' places C before the final A of HARMONIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The glass version of this instrument was a set of tuned glass bowls played with wet fingers.

clue.text: Bonnie Charlie before the offer

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
to tender is to offer

explanation.surface: Bonnie Prince Charlie appears before receiving an offer.
explanation.walkthrough: Bonnie Prince Charlie, Charles Edward Stuart, was the Young Pretender to the British throne.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Edward Stuart claimed the British throne and is called the Young claimant of that title.

clue.text: Look over the water ! It's deceptive

indicators.note: in a down clue the first word sits over the second

parts.note: an eye is a look, as in cast an eye
the wash is water thrown back by a boat

explanation.surface: A warning to look across the water, because appearances deceive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places EYE above WASH in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means nonsense or humbug intended to mislead.

clue.text: Chosen or chooser

parts.note: elect means chosen, as in the president-elect

explanation.surface: A riddle asking whether one is picked or does the picking.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter is someone who picks a candidate at the polls.

clue.text: Looks to the start of free services

indicators.note: only the opening letter of free is taken

parts.note: in tennis an ace is a serve the opponent cannot touch

explanation.surface: Someone eyes the beginning of free services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'services' are tennis serves, winning aces.
explanation.definitionFit: Facial expressions or appearances, as in pulling faces, are looks.

clue.text: Robbed but took it like a lamb

definitions.meaning: had one's wool shorn off, as a sheep does

explanation.surface: Someone was robbed but meekly accepted it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took it like a lamb' reads as meek acceptance, but it is having its wool taken.
explanation.definitionFit: To swindle someone is to strip them as a sheep is stripped of its wool.

clue.text: Dock gate is so with a vessel around

indicators.note: the container word sits around the two short words

parts.note: a can is a container
taken as written

explanation.surface: A harbour gate is described this way, with a ship nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship but means a container, CAN, around IS SO.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the floating gate that closes a dry dock as well as a watertight chamber.

clue.text: Predominantly a submarine hazard ?

parts.note: submarine means beneath the sea, and most of this floating danger lies under the surface

explanation.surface: Something that chiefly endangers submarines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'submarine' looks like the vessel but is the adjective: mostly below the waterline.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughly nine-tenths of a floating mass of ice lies underwater, a danger to shipping.

clue.text: Right shape around the middle

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the measurement taken there, a noun

indicators.note: to shape is to reform, so the letters of right are remade

explanation.surface: The proper figure round the waist.
explanation.definitionFit: The measurement round the waist or belly is a person's circumference.

clue.text: Past the single period

parts.note: one means single
time means a period

explanation.surface: Gone is the period of being single.
explanation.definitionFit: Former, as in a former champion, means past.

clue.text: Kings may love treason, but the. — hate." (Dekker)

definitions.text: Kings may love treason, but the. — hate." (Dekker)

parts.words: Kings may love treason, but the. — hate." (Dekker)
parts.note: the gap is the person who commits treason, whom kings despise even while they profit from the betrayal

explanation.surface: A line from the Jacobean playwright Thomas Dekker with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Dekker's line contrasts the act of betrayal, which rulers welcome, with the betrayer, whom they despise.
explanation.definitionFit: One who commits treason is a betrayer of country or cause.

clue.text: Enamelled cutter

parts.note: a biting tooth coated in enamel, not a decorated blade

explanation.surface: A coated cutting tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enamelled' suggests decorated metalwork, but tooth enamel is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A front tooth used for biting is coated in enamel and cuts food.

clue.text: In the services lay one long pipe

definitions.meaning: a lay officer serving a parish church during worship
a clay tobacco pipe with a very long stem

explanation.surface: A layman in religious services and a long tobacco pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'services' are church services and 'lay' means not ordained.
explanation.definitionFit: The parish's elected lay officer gives his title to the long-stemmed clay pipe.
